sections.title: Reading a play script

options.fb: “stage directions” means words in brackets telling actors what to do.
“scene” means one part of a play in one place.

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 4. In this lesson: Reading a play script.
Understand how a play script is set out and read it aloud.
Here are some new words. Script. The written words of a play. Scene.
One part of a play in one place. Stage directions.
Words in brackets telling actors what to do. Listen and say them. script
scene
stage directions.
And some more words. Audience. The people who watch a play. Rehearse.
Practise a play before the show. Costume. The clothes an actor wears in a play.
Listen and say them. audience
rehearse
costume.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: the written words of a play?
Now some grammar: must and mustn't. Use ‘must’ for things that are necessary.
Use ‘mustn't’ for things that are not allowed. For example: Actors must learn their lines.
For example: You mustn't talk during the show.
Now listen, and read along. The magic paintbrush, Scene 1. Scene 1: A small market.
Ming is selling paintbrushes. An old woman walks in slowly.
Old woman: (tired) Young man, I have no money, but I am very hungry.
Ming: (kindly) Here, take my rice. I can eat later. Old woman: (smiling) You are kind.
Take this paintbrush. Anything you paint will become real.
Ming: (laughing) Real? That's impossible! Ming paints a small bird.
The bird flaps its wings and flies away. Ming: (amazed) It's true!
Another question. The video will stop. Where does Scene 1 take place?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like script, scene, stage directions.
You practised must and mustn't. And you read The magic paintbrush, Scene 1.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 4. In this lesson: Speaking with feeling.
Use adverbs and stage directions to show how characters speak.
Here are some new words. Expression. Showing feelings in your voice and face. Volume.
How loud or quiet a sound is. Pause. Stop for a short time. Listen and say them. expression
volume
pause.
And some more words. Nervous. A bit worried. Confident.
Sure that you can do something well. Bow. Bend forward at the end of a show.
Listen and say them. nervous
confident
bow.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: showing feelings in your voice and face?
Now some grammar: Adverbs for stage directions.
Adverbs tell actors how to say or do something. They often go in brackets.
For example: (angrily) Give it back! For example: (whispering softly) Be quiet.
Now listen, and read along. The magic paintbrush, Scene 2. Scene 2: The palace.
The greedy King sits on his throne. Ming stands in front of him.
King: (loudly) Paint me a mountain of gold!
Ming: (nervously) Your Majesty, the brush only helps people who need it.
King: (angrily) Do it now, or you will go to prison!
Ming: (pausing, then confidently) Very well. He paints a wide sea and a ship.
King: (excited) A ship! I will sail to find gold. The King climbs onto the ship.
Ming paints a strong wind. The ship sails far away.
Ming: (to the audience, smiling) And the greedy king never came back.
Another question. The video will stop. Who sits on the throne?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like expression, volume, pause.
You practised adverbs for stage directions. And you read The magic paintbrush, Scene 2.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
